rationale:
bugs_open/390 (arm 2 of the closed bugs_closed/352). A `contrast_failure` records one unreadable text/background pairing on one page. It is routed to `css-patch-agent`, which APPENDS a rule to the site theme stylesheet and is then stamped `complete` because a rule was WRITTEN. Nothing checks whether the rule took effect.

On the measured population it cannot take effect, and the agent's own PROMPT is the proximate cause. It currently says, verbatim (planted by migration 318): "Rely on the cascade: an appended rule with the same or higher specificity overrides the earlier declaration. Repeat the offending selector exactly as it appears above (or more specifically) so your override wins."

Both halves are false for this agent's actual situation:
 * "as it appears above" - the offending selector does NOT appear above. The model is handed `spec.selector`, the audit's ancestor-derived selector, and the declaration that beats it is not in this stylesheet at all.
 * "the same specificity overrides" - it does not, when the competitor is LATER in source order, and the competitor always is. Page-level <style> blocks live in `page_components.rendered_html`, and `assemblePage` emits them inside <main>, always after the <link> in <head>. That ordering is structural, on every page, and cannot be reordered from this agent.

MEASUREMENT [MEASURED 2026-08-25, and it could have come out otherwise]. 40 random completed findings with real (non-invented) selectors across 7 sites; for each I fetched the served page and served theme and located the governing `color` declaration: 33 in the page block OUT-SPECIFYING the filed selector, 6 in the page block at lower specificity, 0 in the theme, 1 not located. Near-uniform shape: filed `TAG.class` (0,1,1) against page `.section .class` (0,2,0). Worked case, settled at the artefact: vonc.com/index.html, filed `A.gauntlet-btn-primary`, agent appended `A.gauntlet-btn-primary{color:#ffffff}` (0,1,1); the winner is `.gauntlet-cta-section .gauntlet-btn-primary{color:var(--color-primary,#1a1a2e)}` (0,2,0) in an inline <style> at byte 22285. Item is `complete`.

DAMAGE, over site_work_items UNION site_work_items_archive [MEASURED 2026-08-25]: 75 of 151 real-selector (page, selector) pairings that ever reached `complete` were filed AGAIN afterwards; 97 re-filings carry byte-identical fg AND bg. At the artefact the churn is accumulated dead rules: noted.co.uk 16 appended contrast fixes for 5 distinct selectors, vonc.com 53 for 39, loanzy.uk 62 for 31.

THE CHANGE. One migration, one jsonb key, one replace(): the prompt stops instructing the losing move. It states that the declaration to beat is usually not in this stylesheet, that an appended rule is always earlier in source order and therefore can never win on position, and that the model should repeat the audited selector and mark ONLY the single property it is correcting as !important.

WHY !important, IN AN ESTATE THAT AVOIDS IT. This agent's shape is the one shape CSS's escape hatch exists for: an APPEND-ONLY writer to a file that is always earlier in source order than its competitors and never sees them. The two Go precedents avoid !important because each owns a surface this agent lacks - `fix_component_template_action.go:440-444` appends AFTER the slot's own <style> so it wins on order, and `emit_sprite_css_action.go:248` authors both competing rules. Neither option exists here.

The premise is MEASURED, not assumed: page-level colour declarations already carrying !important, across 8 sites' homepages, are 0 of 812 (noted 0/157, idea 0/210, cookly 0/120, vonc 0/94, remortgagecalculator 0/78, oufe 0/72, loanzy 0/42, loancash 0/39). So an appended important colour rule wins today in every measured case. It is a STATE measurement and it expires; the RUNBOOK carries the re-run.

THIS IS THE INTERIM, AND THE FILE SAYS SO. Commit 2 of this lane teaches the render audit to record WHICH declaration wins and where it lives; commit 3 replaces this blanket instruction with that measured requirement, so !important is used only where importance parity actually demands it. The migration header instructs whoever writes commit 3 to assert THIS file's text in its drift guard, not 318's.

SCOPE, STATED HONESTLY. This does not help the ~56% of live inflow that never reaches the prompt (no linked theme -> css_no_theme_198; shared or short theme -> migration 542's base-integrity gate). It does not stop a repair being ERASED - migration 543's persist_css_to_theme rewrites css_themes.css_content byte-for-byte at the site's next design run, taking every appended patch with it (agritec.uk: 5 repairs erased 2026-08-25 12:09:57, items still `complete`); that is filed separately. It does not make `complete` mean the text became readable - that is the completion-gate half, deferred by owner decision 2026-08-25 in favour of fixing the routing first. And it does not repair the underlying palette token; it wins the pairing the audit measured and suppresses no evidence, because every other pairing that token breaks is still filed.

NO ORDERING CONSTRAINT IS CLAIMED (owner ruling 2026-07-29). Config only, live on apply, depends on no unshipped code.

edits.rationale: Tell the runner when this is already applied, so a re-run is a loud no-op rather than a silent second replace. Keys on the new anchor text, not on a step name, because this migration adds no step.
edits.sketch: DO $probe$ BEGIN IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM agent_definitions WHERE type='css-patch-agent' AND is_active AND COALESCE(is_snapshot,false)=false AND deleted_at IS NULL AND default_config #>> '{workflow,steps,plan_css_fix,config,prompt_template}' LIKE '%can never win on position%') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION '390/616: already applied'; END IF; END $probe$;

edits.rationale: README rule: every migration touching agent_definitions opens with a snapshot. It is also what the ROLLBACK file names as the alternative to its inverse replace.

A blind replace() against text that has moved is a SILENT NO-OP that still reports success - the exact failure shape this estate keeps paying for. So: assert plan_css_fix is still an execute_llm_prompt step; assert 318's append is still in place (save_css_to_db params[1] = css_fix.result.css_added), because this migration is meaningless against a workflow that round-trips the whole document; assert the target bullet is present VERBATIM and EXACTLY ONCE. The occurrence count is done by searching twice rather than by dividing a length difference by a hand-typed constant - that constant is a second copy of the sentence's length, drifts from it silently, and I got it wrong (219 for a 214-char string) before replacing the approach.

The change itself. One key, one replace(), dollar-quoted so no escaping is involved. The replacement carries its own evidence (the 39/40 and 33/40 figures, dated) because the next reader of this prompt needs to know the instruction is measured rather than a preference.
edits.sketch: UPDATE agent_definitions SET default_config = jsonb_set(default_config,'{workflow,steps,plan_css_fix,config,prompt_template}', to_jsonb(replace(default_config #>> '{...}', $old$- Rely on the cascade: ...$old$, $new$- IMPORTANT: the declaration you must beat is usually NOT in the stylesheet above. No other property gets !important, and no other property changes.$new$)), false), updated_at=NOW() WHERE type='css-patch-agent' AND is_active AND COALESCE(is_snapshot,false)=false AND deleted_at IS NULL;

edits.rationale: A verify block of plain SELECTs cannot stop a COMMIT - ON_ERROR_STOP ignores a non-empty result - so every post-condition RAISEs. Six: the false instruction is gone; both halves of the correction are present (mechanism AND action, because either alone is useless); the JSON output contract the rest of the workflow reads is intact; the template variables still render; 546's dangling-edge query re-run as a post-condition because this file edits the same row; and 542/546's parks are still wired.

The inverse replace rather than a snapshot restore: 616 changes exactly one key, and a snapshot restore would also discard anything another lane has legitimately changed on this shared row since. The header names the snapshot as the alternative, and states plainly that rolling back REINSTATES a false instruction.
edits.sketch: replace(prompt, $new$...$new$, $old$...$old$) with its own probe guard and RAISE-ing verify.

plan.risks:
1) EXPECTED OBJECTION - '!important is a smell and this estate avoids it.' Answer: the avoidance is justified in both Go precedents by a surface this agent lacks (fix_component_template appends after the competitor; emit_sprite authors both rules). css-patch-agent is an append-only writer to a file that is structurally always earlier and that never sees its competitor, which is the one shape !important exists for. The premise that nothing already competes is MEASURED (0 of 812) rather than assumed, and the migration header says so and dates it.

2) EXPECTED OBJECTION - 'this papers over a palette defect.' Partly true and stated in the header. A pale ink on a pale ground IS a token problem, and bugs_open/296 section 10.5 reaches the same conclusion. But this suppresses no evidence: the audit still measures and files every other pairing the token breaks, and the token fix is site-wide, collides with the palette lane, and 390 section 2 says explicitly not to do it blind. The narrow win is honest about being narrow.

3) !important suppresses state variants on the corrected property - an a:hover recolour on the audited selector will lose. Cosmetic, bounded to one property on a pairing that is currently UNREADABLE, and strictly the lesser harm. A later appended important rule at the same selector supersedes an earlier one (important vs important, equal specificity, source order), so the correction path stays open.

4) PRECEDENT LEAKAGE - 'the estate uses !important now.' Contained by putting the reasoning in the migration header AND in the prompt text itself, scoped to this agent's shape, and by commit 3 replacing the blanket instruction with a measured per-finding requirement.

5) CONCURRENT EDITS to the same live row. Another lane amending css-patch-agent between this file being written and applied would make a blind replace a silent no-op; the drift guard turns that into a loud abort, mutation-proven above.

6) SCOPE HONESTY - this is the cheap interim, not the fix. It cannot make `complete` mean the text became readable (deferred completion gate), cannot help findings that never reach the prompt (~56% of live inflow), and cannot survive a theme re-render (migration 543). All three are named in the header so nobody reads the commit as more than it is.
